description: NovaTerra is a technology-driven team exploring NASA data through AI, scientific computing, data analysis, and interactive visualization. For Planet X and SPHEREx, we focus on temporal astronomical data, change detection, and intuitive scientific visualization. We aim to transform complex datasets into accessible, evidence-based tools that help users explore, understand, and communicate scientific insights.
summary:
The NOVATERRA team's project aims to transform the vast and complex astronomical data collected by NASA's SPHEREx mission into accessible opportunities for scientific exploration for everyone. Given the challenges posed by the enormous volume of astronomical data, including signal noise, difficulties in tracking and comparing celestial changes over time, and the advanced technical expertise required for data processing, our team proposes the development of a user-friendly visualization platform.

The system is designed to automatically retrieve and decode infrared images, optimize data storage, and support the analysis of potential celestial candidates, including hypotheses such as Planet X. Through this approach, the project delivers meaningful contributions to science, education, technology, and society. It empowers students, teachers, astronomy enthusiasts, and the wider community to explore and observe the universe more easily, supports STEM education, and inspires a deeper passion for space exploration and scientific research.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work? NovaTerra is an integrated Global Earth & Sky Digital Twin and scientific exploration platform engineered for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 ("Hunting for Moving Objects with SPHEREx").

It seamlessly bridges geodetic Earth observation, local 3D celestial mechanics, solar/lunar/eclipse observatories, and real-time infrared space mission data. The platform queries NASA/IPAC IRSA via IVOA Table Access Protocol (TAP/ADQL) across 102 spectral channels (0.75 – 5.0 µm) of the SPHEREx mission. It features a custom pure-PHP binary FITS parser (IEEE-754 Big-Endian decoder with ZScale / Asinh stretching), a multi-epoch Blink Comparator ("Time Machine") to detect proper motion displacements, and a difference-imaging candidate detection engine applying 5-sigma outlier thresholds and Planck blackbody Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) fitting (30 K – 70 K) to hunt for outer Solar System candidates (Planet X / Planet Nine).

  1. What benefits does it have?
  • Unified Scientific Foundation: Enforces a single authoritative CelestialState contract across all UI panels, eliminating split-brain calculation discrepancies.
  • Ultra-Portable Zero-SQL Architecture: Runs on standard cPanel/LiteSpeed shared hosting with zero external database dependencies, utilizing atomic file writes, flock concurrency locks, and bounded LRU caches (150 MB).
  • Anti-Hallucination AI Coprocessor: The NOVA Cosmic Mentor operates on a 5-tier grounded architecture where physical facts are hard-coded to NASA NSSDCA / JPL SSD fact sheets, ensuring 100% truthful astronomical guidance without generative hallucinations.
  • Air-Gapped & Offline Reliability: Zero-CDN architecture bundles Three.js r128 locally, supporting full offline usage and resilient fallback modes (including a 2D Canvas engine for hardware without WebGL).
  1. What is the intended impact of the project? NovaTerra democratizes cutting-edge infrared astrophysics and planetary defense. It empowers researchers, students, and citizen scientists worldwide to inspect raw SPHEREx FITS exposures, cross-match multi-epoch infrared surveys (AllWISE, 2MASS, Gaia DR3), and participate in the real-time discovery of fast-moving asteroids, cold brown dwarfs, and hypothetical outer Solar System bodies.
  2. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?
  • Backend: Pure PHP 8.1+ (Zero-SQL, cURL, GD, mbstring, native Binary FitsReader).
  • Frontend / 3D Graphics: JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js r128 (local bundle), HTML5 Canvas, WebGL, custom GLSL shaders (C1 Hermite twilight interpolation, WGS84 ellipsoid quad-ribbon rendering).
  • Space Science Standards: IAU SOFA time synchronization (UTC, TAI, TT, UT1, DUT1, ΔT = 69.184s, GMST/GAST), SGP4 orbital propagation with Earth Umbra shadow evaluation, Meeus astronomical algorithms, and Espenak Besselian eclipse polynomials.
  • Testing & Verification: 4,064 automated PHP unit/integration tests (100% pass rate) and 51 Headless Chrome E2E responsive test suites.
  1. How is your project creative? NovaTerra unites terrestrial geography and deep-space astrophysics into a single living digital twin. Features like the Geodesic Observer Jump allow users to click any eclipse on Earth and instantaneously transport their 3D perspective to the totality path with the telescope aligned to the Sun. Furthermore, our Blink Comparator digitizes Clyde Tombaugh's historical Pluto discovery technique into a modern, responsive web tool that compares SPHEREx and AllWISE infrared epochs side-by-side.
  2. What factors did your team consider? Our team prioritized the 8-tier Engineering Priority Chain established in our project Constitution: Scientific Accuracy > Functional Correctness > Data Integrity > Architectural Consistency > Reliability/Security > Runtime Performance > User Experience > Visual Polish. We strictly adhered to the "Zero-Fabrication Law" (clearly separating simulated candidates from real IRSA observations) and addressed all 9 critical hackathon pitfalls (including SSRF defense, proper uncertainty propagation, and end-to-end SHA-256 provenance).
